newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes soft, grades mellow after sour spurt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes soft, grades mellow after sour spurt.

text.p: U.S. crudes headed into the final push for Wednesday business on a weaker note, pressured by technical selling and moderate temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, traders said.
Cash dealers said grade action had died down after a very busy morning, which featured a strong sour market due to production problems at key platforms offshore Louisiana.
"I think with the problems in the Gulf, a lot of people got caught short," said a trader, on the sour grade rally.
January West Texas Sour firmed to trade at only a $1.00 discount to the Jan West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark.
Crude's Jan WTI/Cushing marker was currently tracked 40 cts lower at $25.25-35 a barrel, but some 30 cts above the session lows around $25.00 a barrel.

Mobil announced earlier Wednesday that its Green Canyon platform in the Gulf of Mexico would be out of service for two to three months as a result of a fire at the facility last week. The platform produces around 21,800 barrels per day (bpd) of oil and 43 million cubi feet per day of natural gas.
Major refiners were heard buying up the WTS market, filling sour supply needs in lieu of the platform shutdown and the short holiday week in the offing next week.
Other grades were talked slighty weaker to steady, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at 45-50 cts over the WTI/Cushing and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire 10-15 cts over.
